objectives.description: Attribute both suites' wall clock on a quiet host before changing anything: per-invocation timing for every nested verify-deploy.sh call, written to progress/

Narrow test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's baseline capture to --max-cost moderate (establish it does not need gate 3/22's own findings, since those are covered elsewhere); scope the header to match
Split test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh's case(b) (23-gate standalone crash net, not narrowable) into its own suite, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection-crash-net.sh, for scheduling

Assess whether any remaining nested invocation can be replaced by a direct assertion against the gate's own script -- recorded as not applicable (dominated by wrapper overhead; several calls deliberately test the wrapper's own mechanisms)

Update the three affected suite-cost-hints.txt rows from this phase's own direct measurements (full --regen-hints deferred to Phase 13, out of this single-phase dispatch's budget); correct run-all.sh's stale rejected-alternatives figure

approaches_tried.approach: Instrumenting a TEMPORARY COPY of each suite (never the original, never committed) with timing prints wrapped around run_vd()/the standalone verify-deploy.sh calls, run from the real scripts/tests/ directory under a non-test-*.sh-matching filename, then deleted immediately after capture
approaches_tried.reason: Running the copy from a scratch tmpdir broke its own SCRIPT_DIR/CORE_DIR-relative path resolution (the suite expects to find verify-deploy.sh at a fixed relative offset from its own location); running it in-place under a name run-all.sh's discovery glob would not match, then deleting it immediately, gave accurate per-invocation timing with zero risk of the scratch file being discovered or committed.

approaches_tried.approach: First timing-wrapper draft dropped run_vd()'s own exit code (the wrapped function's last statement became `printf '%s' "$_out"`, always rc=0)
approaches_tried.reason: Two cases that assert a specific non-zero exit code (case f, case h) failed under the instrumented copy even though the UNDERLYING verify-deploy.sh behavior was unchanged -- an artifact of the instrumentation, not a real regression. Fixed by capturing $? explicitly after the command substitution and `return`-ing it from the wrapper.

approaches_tried.approach: Reproducing the context-budget suite's fixture with `git add -A` / a bare directory pathspec inside a disposable scratch git repo, to measure the baseline call in isolation
approaches_tried.reason: guard-destructive-git.sh's over-staging predicate is a pure command-text match with no cwd-awareness -- it refuses `git add -A` and any bare-directory pathspec regardless of which repository the command targets, including a throwaway /tmp scratch repo unrelated to the project. Worked around via `find -type f -print0 | xargs -0 git add --`, which stages an explicit file list (the form the guard is designed to require) rather than a directory/glob pathspec.

approaches_tried.approach: Measuring the context-budget baseline's own A/B cost (full battery vs --max-cost moderate) by reproducing its exact fixture (rsync + CLAUDE.md/.claude-extensions.json/.gitignore + symlinked .claude + git init/add/commit) once, then running both verify-deploy.sh invocations back-to-back against the identical fixture state
approaches_tried.reason: Clean, reusable fixture avoided re-paying the ~300ms build cost per measurement and guaranteed both arms of the A/B saw byte-identical input: 159,191ms (full battery) vs 25,222ms (--max-cost moderate), an 84% cut with the same finding set on every gate the moderate selection still covers.

deviations.description: Regenerate both suites' hints via measure-gate-costs.sh --regen-hints
deviations.reason: --regen-hints re-measures the ENTIRE ~150-suite pool (averaged across multiple runs), a multi-minute-to-tens-of-minutes operation out of proportion to a single-phase dispatch's budget. A full regeneration is deferred to Phase 13, which already lists suite-cost-hints.txt in its own files-to-modify for exactly this final-regeneration purpose.
